options.label: Commit a setup script
options.description: Add scripts/install-twsapi.sh to dstrader that extracts com/ib from dstrader-docker's DSTrader.jar and mvn install:install-file's it, + SETUP.md docs. No binaries committed; reproducible from artifacts you already have. (Recommended)

options.label: Vendor the jar in-repo
options.description: Commit twsapi-10.19.03.jar (227K) into dstrader (e.g. lib/) and point the pom at a local file repository, so `mvn` builds with zero setup. Self-contained, but commits IB's binary into the repo.

options.label: Document IB official source
options.description: Just document in SETUP.md how to get twsapi from IB's official TWS API download (the canonical origin) and install it. Most 'correct', but each builder must do the IB download step.

questions.question: What about the 548M local toolchain + temp junk?

options.label: Delete tarballs + /tmp only
options.description: Remove the 209M of *.tar.gz and /tmp/twsapi-extract, but KEEP the working JDK/Maven + twsapi in .m2 so I (or you) can rebuild locally without re-downloading. (Recommended)

options.label: Remove everything
options.description: Delete ~/.local/toolchain entirely and the twsapi from ~/.m2. Frees 548M; a future build re-downloads/re-installs via the repo script.

options.label: Leave it all
options.description: Keep everything as-is, including the tarballs and temp dir.

Good question — let me inventory exactly what I created/touched that lives **outside** version control, then we can decide what belongs in a repo.

Here's the precise inventory. Only the **merged code** is in a repo right now; everything else I created during the build/verify is machine-local:

| Outside a repo | Where | Size | Nature |
|---|---|---|---|
| JDK 21 + Maven binaries | `~/.local/toolchain/` | 548M (209M is the two `*.tar.gz`) | Downloaded binaries |
| Reconstructed **twsapi** jar+pom | `~/.m2/repository/com/ib/twsapi/10.19.03/` | ~228K | Local Maven cache — **the real reproducibility gap** |
| Temp extraction | `/tmp/twsapi-extract/` | 1.2M | Disposable |
| Build how-to | agent memory `reference_dstrader_java_build.md` | — | Knowledge, not versioned |

Two of these you'd **never** put in a repo (a 548M JDK/Maven, IB's binary jar). What genuinely *should* be in a repo is the **reproducibility**: today a fresh clone of `dstrader` can't compile at all, because `com.ib:twsapi:10.19.03` resolves from nowhere — it only exists because I hand-installed it. That gap is what "all in repos" should fix.

The natural home is `dstrader/docs/SETUP.md` (it exists). I'll add a "Building & testing" section there regardless. The open decision is **how** to make twsapi resolvable from the repo:
